scope: Actual opt-in App preview ownership through the existing original public runtime/Host and context actor; production route and full C2/C3/C4 acceptance remain unfinished.
implementation: Same LegadoMainJSSourceService actor, existing source acquire/release/waiter deadlines, context directory and JSON file category. No new file library, queue, state cache, JSContext, JVM, HTTP transport or Cookie jar.
V1 mainJs record/reference types and 34 existing function groups preserve their exact source bytes. AppLegadoBookStateOwner source and the real App bindBook/Shelf/Chapter predicates stay unchanged.

New explicit Fetcher embedding entry points call originalSearch/details/TOC/content through NativeLegadoOriginalPreviewExecutor, the one LegadoRuntimeProcess, and the actual public typed OriginalTraditionalRuntime API. Public content still encodes needSave=false.

Native original sessions explicitly select existing jvm-okhttp/original-traditional/app-owner-text with one real Host grant; option choice has a prepared assertion and is not reported as JNI or App execution.

Source UUID/revision, exact UTF-8 book URL, actual context record ID, absolute deadline and unique actual runtime taskID bind a private-init preview grant. Imported JSON cannot manufacture a library UUID or a Host grant.

The same Host entity lease table routes App proofs to the unchanged App owner and preview proofs to the existing context actor. Entity callbacks do not reacquire the lock held by their awaiting business call.

TOC-only discovery may read/commit chapter state before the actual returned TOC exists, strictly within that one source/book/context. Content then requires stored chapter UUID/index/exact URL/next URL; no chapter download/save generation is granted.

Small raw DTO variable maps and independent original big-variable companion values persist in one context record. Direct setter result fields commit only when the current raw file revision/SHA still matches this task initial or last accepted Host write proof.

Context reads use one owned O_NOFOLLOW regular FD, an 8 MiB pre-allocation budget, chunked pread cancellation checks, before/after fstat plus path identity checks, and a checked exactly-once close before decoding. Entire chapter identities/indexes/exact URL uniqueness are checked before any array access or unique-key dictionary.

Raw URL bytes encode chapter-state keys to avoid Swift canonical Unicode equality aliasing distinct original Java URL strings. Existing preview chapter UUIDs survive unchanged/reordered URL identities.
Successful Host commits remain after a later business error. Atomic context writes derive their acceptance proof from written bytes with no post-write readback; unchanged records do not rewrite.

Explicit revoke records revoked state for reopening. Transfer requires an existing App UUID/source/book/TOC and matching actual chapter variables, writes transferring intent before original BookStore CAS, then verifies the current App identity and closes the preview. A real failed App replacement preserves old App bytes and a non-writable retryable context intent; reopening resumes only the same UUID.

The canonical Cookie text/read dispatch functions, all five cookieCancellation references and source bind/revoke functions are preserved in the a848-based future Host. Only entity backing/proof dispatch and new bindPreview/task checking differ.

limitations: All 12 new and 42 related Swift methods are prepared selections only. No Apple SDK build/typecheck/test or JNI/App execution was run; six-source grammar diagnostics and source preservation hashes are not runtime acceptance.

Default App search/details/TOC/content route remains unchanged. The existing UI has no newly enabled original route; the explicit embedding APIs are ready for controlled route integration after SDK verification.
Future Cookie WebKit/clear/cache actions are a separate owner stage. Root must merge later Host diffs semantically, never copy this entire file over a newer Cookie stage.
Local CAS serialization is guaranteed only by one injected existing context actor. No cross-process or independently instantiated concurrent-owner transaction is promised.
A reopening caller must retain its existing context reference. No new cold-UI navigation restoration index or scan of user context files is introduced.
Source changes/revoke/cancel follow these explicit embedding APIs and existing Host lifecycle; this work does not claim a new global App source-edit observer or default route lifecycle.

Transfer rejects changed App chapter variables or variable compartments the current App owner cannot represent. It does not overwrite existing App chapter state or bypass its generation predicates to repair a mismatch.

Transfer spans two existing owners and is resumable, not atomic across files. An error after a successful App CAS can leave that genuine partial write plus the transferring intent; it is never reported as a complete receipt.
Preview HTML/media rendering, content caching/download publication, complete App identity mapping, full book-source compatibility and whole C2/C3/C4 acceptance remain unfinished.
